finding: Magnetic-field cross-body four-axis test of unified hypothesis: gauge-field-compression (d_geom-driven) is magnetic-field DRIVER while iron/metallic-H/plasma is CONDUCTOR; f-term has cosmic-substrate-saturation threshold that crossed in 4.4-3.5 Ga window, marooning small bodies. Four-axis discriminator: AXIS 1 tripartition-shadow multipole; AXIS 2 d_geom monotone dependence; AXIS 3 f vs g x h three-corner; AXIS 4 cosmic-epoch clustering vs cooling-timescale.

AXIS 1 — Tripartition-shadow multipole test on 5 bodies (Sun, Mercury, Earth, Jupiter, Saturn). Mean M2/M1 = 0.293 +/- 0.211; Mean M3/M1 = 0.300 +/- 0.307; Mean M3/M2 = 1.204 +/- 0.870. Paired t (H0: M3/M1 = M2/M1) = 0.07, df=4, n.s. 3 of 5 bodies have M3 > M2 (Sun, Jupiter, Saturn); 2 have M3 < M2 (Mercury outlier with M3/M2 = 0.125; Earth with 0.643). Hidden stratification signal: log(M3/M2) vs log(d_geom) Pearson r = 0.69 (n=5, t=1.63, p~0.10 one-tailed). Tripartition-shadow NOT detected at p<0.05 at this operationalisation and sample size.

finding: AXIS 2 — d_geom monotone regression on 6 active-dynamo bodies. log(B_dipole) vs log(d_geom) Pearson r = 0.7720; t = 2.429 (df=4); p<0.05 one-tailed; p>0.05 two-tailed. Linear regression slope = 0.552, R² = 0.596. Within-iron stratification (Mercury, Earth, Ganymede n=3): Pearson r = 0.890 — strong correlation even after conductor control. Within metallic-H (Jupiter, Saturn n=2): two-point slope = 2.876. Iron-only sorted by d_geom shows Earth (largest d_geom) has clearly highest B, but Ganymede-Mercury ordering not strictly monotone. Effect spans 6 OOM in d_geom and 4 OOM in B.

finding: AXIS 3 — f vs g x h discrimination via OLS model comparison. Model A: log(B) ~ a + c*I_metallicH + d*I_plasma (no d_geom) -> R² = 0.540. Model B: + b*log(d_geom) -> R² = 0.909. R² improvement +0.369. F-statistic for added d_geom = 8.14 (df=1,2); below critical F=18.5 at n=6 small-sample. Iron-only Pearson r = 0.890. Iron-fit extrapolation OVER-predicts (not under-predicts) Sun by 5.2 OOM, Jupiter by 1.3 OOM, Saturn by 1.8 OOM. Conclusion: simple slope-1.65 iron extrapolation does not work cross-conductor; conductors carry intrinsic g-multipliers (iron > metallic-H > plasma in field-strength-at-same-d_geom). BUT once conductor is one-hot encoded, d_geom contributes substantial fit beyond g x h (R² 0.54 -> 0.91). Venus consistency check: both standard and framework predict zero field (no convection); not a discriminator.

finding: AXIS 4 — Cosmic-epoch clustering vs cooling-timescale on 3 lost-field bodies (Moon 3.5 Ga, Mars 3.8 Ga, Vesta 3.9 Ga). Cooling-timescale-proxy range: 5 to 400 Myr = 80x spread (Vesta 5 Myr, Moon 30 Myr, Mars 400 Myr). Body-age-at-loss range: 660 to 1000 Myr = 1.52x spread. Compression ratio 53x. Standard cooling-model scaling check: c = body_age_at_loss / cooling_proxy varies 75x across bodies (Moon 33.3, Mars 1.75, Vesta 132). Under standard model c should be constant; observed 75x spread directly rejects proportional cooling scaling. Field-loss CV = 5.6%; cooling-proxy CV = 152.5%. Spearman rank correlations: r(cooling_proxy, field_loss_Ga) = -0.50; r(radius, field_loss_Ga) = -0.50. Caveats: n=3; Late Heavy Bombardment (4.0-3.8 Ga) is a competing astrophysical explanation overlapping the field-loss window; tidal heating, impact gardening confound.
anchor_class: cosmic-epoch threshold framework prediction; cooling-timescale standard prediction rejected at effect-size level
